Apple Fennel Slaw is crisp, fresh, sweet, and tangy with crunchy pecans and a bright honey-Dijon dressing. It is SO good!

Author’s Notes

Meet My New Favorite Slaw: Apple Fennel

WOW, this slaw! I am beyond excited to share this recipe with you. It is honestly my new favorite slaw, and I am 1000% bringing it to every function I can these next few months because it is THAT good

I started working on it right after I got home from London as part of a bigger project: recreating The Black Pig’s iconic sandwich from Borough Market. I have raved about that sandwich for years and still think it is one of the best sandwiches I’ve ever had, so I decided it was high time I figured out how to make my own version at home.

The sandwich has turned into a bigger project than I expected, and somehow the slaw was one of the trickiest parts to nail down. That is, until THIS recipe.

This is exactly how I remember it. Crisp, fresh, a little sweet, and good enough to completely stand on its own, with a dressing I could honestly drink. I knew immediately it deserved its own spotlight here.

And yes, that sandwich is still coming! But in the meantime, make this apple fennel slaw because OH MAN. It is so, so good.

Apple Fennel Slaw Ingredients

Chelsea’s Tips

Tips For Making Apple Fennel Slaw

  • Use a mandoline for the fennel, apples, and cabbage: It gives you those really thin, even slices that make the slaw so much better. Always use the hand guard, especially once the vegetable starts getting small!
  • Cut the fennel in half first: Remove the stalks, slice through the bulb, then cut out the tough core before slicing through the mandolin.
  • Dress gradually: Start with most of the dressing, toss well, then add more only if needed. It’s easier to add than fix an overdressed slaw!

Storage

Once dressed, this apple fennel slaw is best enjoyed the same day.

Apple Fennel Slaw

By Chelsea Lords
Apple Fennel Slaw is fresh, bright, and full of crunch with tart apples, fennel, pecans, and the BEST honey-Dijon dressing.
Recipe adapted from Ottolenghi
Prep Time: 30 minutes minutes
Total Time: 30 minutes minutes
Servings: 8 servings, as a side

Equipment

  • Large bowl
  • Mandoline slicer

Ingredients

Dressing
  • 1/2 teaspoon fennel seeds optional
  • 3 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
  • 3 tablespoons honey
  • 1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon Dijon-style mustard
  • 1 large lemon zested all over plus 1 tbsp juice
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
  • 1/4 cup + 3 tablespoons olive oil extra-virgin
  • 3/4 teaspoon fine sea salt
For the Slaw
  • 7 cups lightly packed cabbage from 1 small 12-ounce cabbage
  • 3 cups very thinly sliced fennel from 1 large bulb
  • 2 cups very thinly sliced granny smith apples and cut into matchsticks (1-2 apples)
  • 1 pkt fresh dill roughly chopped
  • 3/4 cup candied pecans coarsely chopped

Instructions 

  • Chill ingredients: For the most refreshing slaw, chill all the ingredients before assembling.
  • Make the dressing: If using fennel seeds, crush them in a mortar and pestle or place them in a bag and crush with a meat mallet or heavy skillet. Add to a wide-mouth mason jar with the remaining dressing ingredients. Secure the lid and shake well until emulsified. Set aside until ready to use. The dressing can be made ahead; just shake again before using if it separates.
  • Prep the cabbage: Cut the cabbage into quarters and remove the core. Thinly slice with a mandoline. Wash well and dry thoroughly (I like to use a salad spinner).
  • Prep the fennel: Remove the stalks and fronds, trim out the tough core, then very thinly slice the bulb with a mandoline.
  • Prep the apples: Thinly slice the apples with a mandoline, then cut the slices into thin matchsticks. Transfer to a bowl of cold water, sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt, and gently stir. Let stand for 10 minutes, then drain in a colander and rinse well with cold water. Dry thoroughly. This helps keep the apples from browning.
  • Assemble: Add the cabbage, fennel, apples, and dill to a large bowl. Add the dressing gradually and toss well, adding more as needed. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
  • Finish: Top with the candied pecans and serve right away.
Final step! Please let us know how it was by leaving a review.

Recipe Notes

Storage: This slaw can be stored for up to 1 day, but once dressed, it is best within an hour or so.
